disease_label_per_paper: Multi-phasic life-threatening anaphylaxis refractory to epinephrine managed by ECMO
presentation_summary: A 52-year-old patient without known allergies developed sudden respiratory distress prehospital.
Paramedics found SpO2 87%, respiratory rate 20/min, BP 90/50 mmHg, and heart rate 120/min.
In the ED, SpO2 deteriorated to 83% despite oxygen 15 L/min; norepinephrine and noninvasive support failed, and she was intubated and switched to continuous epinephrine infusion.
After CT she developed flush/urticaria, red conjunctivas, and respiratory instability and was treated for suspected anaphylaxis with steroids and diphenhydramine.
Thirty minutes later she deteriorated again to BP 70/47 mmHg, and another episode around 9 PM caused flushing, severe bronchospasm, and hemodynamic instability despite high-dose epinephrine.
VA-ECMO was initiated for hemodynamic support; day 2 included further severe bouts of anaphylaxis with ventilation nearly impossible.
Tryptase levels were reported as more than 50-fold the upper normal limit; later workup showed KIT D816V mutation and bone marrow findings diagnosing indolent systemic mastocytosis.
